title: Tiere & Farben (Animals & Colours)
description: Name animals and pets, learn the colours, describe animals with sein, form your first plurals, and say what you like and dislike.

notes.heading: 📌 Animals (Die Tiere)
notes.body:
**das Tier** = the animal. Here are the most useful animal words:

| German | English |
|---|---|
| der Hund | the dog |
| die Katze | the cat |
| der Vogel | the bird |
| der Fisch | the fish |
| das Pferd | the horse |
| die Kuh | the cow |
| das Schwein | the pig |
| das Schaf | the sheep |
| das Kaninchen | the rabbit |
| der Bär | the bear |
| der Löwe | the lion |
| der Elefant | the elephant |
| der Affe | the monkey |
| die Schlange | the snake |
| die Maus | the mouse |

Learn each animal with its article: der, die or das is part of the word.

notes.heading: 📌 Talking About Pets (Haustiere)
notes.body:
**das Haustier** = the pet. The key question is:

**Hast du ein Haustier?** — Do you have a pet?

Possible answers:
- Ja, ich habe ein**en** Hund. — Yes, I have a dog.
- Ja, ich habe ein**e** Katze. — Yes, I have a cat.
- Ja, ich habe zwei Kaninchen. — Yes, I have two rabbits.
- Nein, ich habe **kein** Haustier. — No, I have no pet.

Notice what happens after **haben**: masculine words change ein → **einen** and der → **den** (Ich habe einen Hund / Ich sehe den Hund). This is the **accusative case** — it marks the thing the action happens to. Feminine (eine Katze), neuter (ein Pferd) and plural words do not change.

To say you would like one: *Ich möchte einen Hund.* — I would like a dog.

notes.heading: 🔑 Colours (Die Farben)
notes.body:
**die Farbe** = the colour.

| German | English |
|---|---|
| rot | red |
| blau | blue |
| grün | green |
| gelb | yellow |
| schwarz | black |
| weiß | white |
| braun | brown |
| orange | orange |
| rosa | pink |
| lila | purple |
| grau | grey |

Make colours lighter or darker with **hell-** and **dunkel-**:
- hellblau — light blue
- dunkelgrün — dark green

**Welche Farbe hat...?** — What colour is...? *Welche Farbe hat dein Fahrrad? — Es ist rot.*

Spelling watch: weiß takes the ß (it rhymes with heiß), and after sein, colours never change their form: *Die Katze ist schwarz.*

notes.heading: 🔑 Describing with sein: Der Hund ist braun
notes.body:
The simplest German description uses **sein** (to be) + adjective:

- Der Hund **ist** braun. — The dog is brown.
- Die Katze **ist** schwarz. — The cat is black.
- Das Pferd **ist** groß. — The horse is big.
- Die Fische **sind** bunt. — The fish are colourful.

**The golden rule:** after sein, the adjective takes **NO ending** — ist braun, ist groß, sind klein.

When the adjective stands directly **before a noun**, it takes an ending (usually -e at this level):
- der braun**e** Hund — the brown dog
- ein**e** schwarz**e** Katze — a black cat
- ein klein**es** Schwein — a small pig

Useful describing words: groß (big), klein (small), schnell (fast), langsam (slow), süß (cute/sweet), gefährlich (dangerous), laut (loud), müde (tired).

notes.heading: 🔑 Plural Patterns (Der Plural)
notes.body:
German plurals follow a handful of patterns. **All** of them take the article **die**:

| Pattern | Example |
|---|---|
| add -e | der Hund → die Hund**e**, das Pferd → die Pferd**e** |
| add -en / -n | die Katze → die Katze**n**, die Schlange → die Schlang**en** |
| no change | der Vogel → die Vogel, das Schwein → die Schweine (this one adds -e!) |
| add -er (+ umlaut) | das Kind → die Kind**er**, das Haus → die Häus**er** |
| umlaut only | die Maus → die M**äu**se, die Kuh → die K**ü**he |

There is no single rule that tells you which pattern a noun uses — learn the plural when you learn the word, just like the gender.

Remember the verb changes too: **Der Hund ist** braun → **Die Hunde sind** braun. (ist → sind in the plural)

notes.heading: 💡 Likes & Dislikes (Vorlieben)
notes.body:
Two easy ways to say what you like:

**1. mögen (to like):**
- Ich **mag** Hunde. — I like dogs.
- Ich mag **keine** Spinnen. — I do not like spiders. (keine = no, for the negative)
- Magst du Katzen? — Do you like cats?

**2. gern haben (to be fond of):**
- Ich **habe** Pferde **gern**. — I am fond of horses.
- Ich habe Schlangen **nicht gern**. — I do not like snakes.

Give a reason with **weil** (because) — the verb goes to the very end:
- Ich mag Hunde, **weil** sie so treu **sind**. — I like dogs because they are so loyal.
- Ich mag Spinnen nicht, **weil** sie gruselig **sind**. — I do not like spiders because they are creepy.

To ask about favourites: **Was ist dein Lieblingstier?** — What is your favourite animal? *Mein Lieblingstier ist der Delfin.*

notes.heading: ⚠️ Common Mistakes with Animals & Colours
notes.body:
1. **Adding endings after sein** — say *Der Hund ist braun*, never *Der Hund ist braune*. Endings only appear before a noun: der braune Hund.
2. **Forgetting weiß has ß** — *weiss* is only acceptable in Switzerland; in standard German it is weiß.
3. **Plural article** — every plural is die: die Hunde, die Katzen, die Tiere. Never der or das in the plural.
4. **Forgetting the plural verb** — Die Fische **sind** bunt, not *Die Fische ist bunt*.
5. **Lower-case nouns** — Tiere, Farben, Hund, Katze all need capitals, wherever they stand in the sentence.

✅ Check yourself: *Ich mag die schwarzen Katzen, weil sie so elegant sind.* — plural article die, adjective ending -en before the plural noun, verb at the end after weil. All correct!

flashcards.example: Der Hund ist groß und braun. — The dog is big and brown.
Die Katze schläft auf dem Sofa. — The cat is sleeping on the sofa.
Das Pferd ist sehr schnell. — The horse is very fast.
Der Vogel singt am Morgen. — The bird sings in the morning.
Der Fisch schwimmt im Wasser. — The fish swims in the water.
Die Schlange ist lang und grün. — The snake is long and green.
Der Löwe ist gefährlich. — The lion is dangerous.
Das Auto ist rot. — The car is red.
Der Himmel ist blau. — The sky is blue.
Meine Katze ist schwarz. — My cat is black.
Der Schnee ist weiß. — The snow is white.

flashcards.definition: I like... (mögen = to like; negative: Ich mag keine...)
flashcards.example: Ich mag Hunde, aber ich mag keine Spinnen. — I like dogs, but I do not like spiders.

questions.stem: What is die Katze in English?
questions.explanation: Die Katze is the cat. The dog is der Hund, the cow is die Kuh and the rabbit is das Kaninchen.
Rot is red. Blue is blau, yellow is gelb and pink is rosa.

questions.stem: Der Hund ist braun — what does this sentence mean?
questions.explanation: Ist is the verb (is), so this is a full sentence: The dog is brown. The brown dog without a verb would be der braune Hund, with an -e ending on the adjective.

questions.stem: Which of these animals is a typical Haustier (pet)?
questions.explanation: Der Hamster is a hamster — a classic small pet. Lions, elephants and bears are wild animals (Wildtiere) that you would only see in a zoo.
Weiß (spelled with ß) is the colour white. Grey is grau. The similar-looking English words wide and wise are false trails — the German words are weit and weise.

questions.stem: What is the plural of die Katze?
questions.explanation: Feminine nouns typically add -n or -en in the plural: die Katze → die Katzen, like die Schlange → die Schlangen.

questions.stem: What is the plural of das Schwein (the pig)?
questions.explanation: Das Schwein → die Schweine follows the -e pattern (like der Hund → die Hunde). Remember that every plural takes die, whatever the singular article was.

questions.stem: Die Maus ist ___ — which form of the adjective grau is correct here?
questions.explanation: After the verb sein, adjectives never take an ending: Die Maus ist grau. The -e ending only appears when the adjective stands before a noun: die graue Maus.

questions.stem: Ich mag keine Spinnen — what is this person saying?
choices: I am afraid of my spider.
questions.explanation: With mögen, the negative is kein: Ich mag keine Spinnen = I do not like spiders. Ich habe keine Spinnen would mean I have no spiders.
Fische is plural, so it needs the plural article die and the plural verb sind: Die Fische sind bunt. Singular would be Der Fisch ist bunt.

questions.stem: Mein Fahrrad ist hellblau — what colour is the bike?
questions.explanation: Hell- makes a colour lighter, so hellblau is light blue. Dark blue would be dunkelblau.

questions.stem: What is the plural of die Maus (the mouse)?
questions.explanation: Die Maus → die Mäuse changes the vowel with an umlaut and adds -e. The same pattern gives die Kuh → die Kühe and das Haus → die Häuser.

questions.stem: Which sentence puts the adjective in the correct form before the noun?
questions.explanation: Die Katze is feminine, so it keeps eine, and an adjective before the noun takes -e: eine schwarze Katze. Ein and einen are for neuter and masculine nouns, and schwarz without an ending is only correct after sein.

questions.stem: Mein Lieblingstier ist der Elefant, weil er so groß ist — what does this mean?
choices: My favourite animal is the elephant because it is so big.
My favourite animal is the elephant, but it is too big.
The elephant is my favourite animal and it is grey.
I like elephants when they are big.
questions.explanation: Weil means because and sends the verb (ist) to the end: weil er so groß ist = because it is so big. Das Lieblingstier is the favourite animal.

questions.stem: Which sentence describes several snakes correctly?
choices: Die Schlangen ist grün und gelb.
Die Schlange sind grün und gelb.
Die Schlangen sind grün und gelb.
Der Schlangen sind grün und gelb.
questions.explanation: Several snakes = plural: die Schlange → die Schlangen, with the plural article die and the plural verb sind. Colours after sein take no ending: grün und gelb.
